arxiv-2106-00234.title: From ETH to algebraic relaxation of OTOCs in systems with conserved quantities
arxiv-2106-00234.creator: Vinitha Balachandran, Giuliano Benenti, Giulio Casati, Dario Poletti
arxiv-2106-00234.description: Abstract The relaxation of out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs) has been studied as a mean to characterize the scrambling properties of a quantum system. We show that the presence of local conserved quantities typically results in, at the fastest, an algebraic relaxation of the OTOC provided (i) the dynamics is local and (ii) the system follows the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis.

arxiv-2207-03031.title: FedHeN: Federated Learning in Heterogeneous Networks
arxiv-2207-03031.creator: Durmus Alp Emre Acar, Venkatesh Saligrama
arxiv-2207-03031.description: Abstract We propose a novel training recipe for federated learning with heterogeneous networks where each device can have different architectures. We introduce training with a side objective to the devices of higher complexities to jointly train different architectures in a federated setting.

arxiv-2301-10029.creator: D. Afraz, R. Lashkaripour and M. Bakherad

arxiv-2309-09517.title: FedGKD: Unleashing the Power of Collaboration in Federated Graph Neural Networks
arxiv-2309-09517.creator: Qiying Pan, Ruofan Wu, Tengfei Liu, Tianyi Zhang, Yifei Zhu, Weiqiang Wang
arxiv-2309-09517.description: Abstract . Federated training of Graph Neural Networks (GNN) has become popular in recent years due to its ability to perform graph-related tasks under data isolation scenarios while preserving data privacy. However, graph heterogeneity issues in federated GNN systems continue to pose challenges.

arxiv-2408-08390.title: An Implicit Function Method for Computing the Stability Boundaries of Hill’s Equation
arxiv-2408-08390.creator: Karthik Chikmagalur, Bassam Bamieh
arxiv-2408-08390.description: Abstract Hill’s equation is a common model of a time-periodic system that can undergo parametric resonance for certain choices of system parameters. For most kinds of parametric forcing, stable regions in its two-dimensional parameter space need to be identified numerically, typically by applying a matrix trace criterion.

arxiv-2506-11250.title: Can Time-Series Foundation Models Perform Building Energy Management Tasks? Journal: Data/Math Publication type: ARTICLE TYPE
arxiv-2506-11250.creator: Ozan Baris Mulayim *, Pengrui Quan *, Liying Han, Xiaomin Ouyang, Dezhi Hong, Mario Bergés, Mani Srivastava
arxiv-2506-11250.description: Abstract Building energy management (BEM) tasks require processing and learning from a variety of time-series data. Existing solutions rely on bespoke task- and data-specific models to perform these tasks, limiting their broader applicability. Inspired by the transformative success of Large Language Models (LLMs), Time-Series Foundation Models (TSFMs), trained on diverse datasets, have the potential to change this.

pmc-10568391.title: Ethical and Information Governance Considerations for Promoting Digital Social Interventions in Primary Care
pmc-10568391.creator: Georgios Dimitrios Karampatakis, Helen E Wood, Chris J Griffiths, Nathan C Lea, Richard E Ashcroft, Bill Day, Neil Walker, Neil S Coulson, Anna De Simoni, Tiffany Leung, Danielle Arigo, Evalill Nilsson, Eddie Donaghy, Megan Prictor, Shanshan Guo
pmc-10568391.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Promoting online peer support beyond the informal sector to statutory health services requires ethical considerations and evidence-based knowledge about its impact on patients, health care professionals, and the wider health care system. Evidence on the effectiveness of digital interventions in primary care is sparse, and definitive guidance is lacking on the ethical concerns arising from the use of social media as a means for health-related interventions and research.

pmc-11664661.title: Comparing Intraoperative and Postoperative Complications of Shape-Memory Nitinol Staples for Arthrodesis Across the Midfoot and Hindfoot
pmc-11664661.creator: Abhinav R Balu, John M Dalloul, Peter C Shen, Rachel Bergman, Shaun Chang, Armen Kelikian, Milap Patel, Anish R Kadakia, Muhammad Y Mutawakkil
pmc-11664661.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Category:Midfoot/Forefoot; HindfootIntroduction/Purpose:Shape-memory nitinol staples are an increasingly common construct used for arthrodesis of the foot. In evaluating this new construct, a comprehensive understanding of the various complications associated with staple arthrodesis is necessary in addition to overall fusion outcomes.

pmc-12426110.title: Impact of obesity on clinical outcomes of v-NOTES hysterectomy: a retrospective study
pmc-12426110.creator: Liu Yang, Wang Qilin, Lian Haiying, Pan Feng, Li Tao, Li Junqiang
pmc-12426110.description: BackgroundObesity is a global health challenge that complicates gynecological surgery. Vaginal natural orifice transluminal endoscopic surgery (v-NOTES) offers a minimally invasive approach to total hysterectomy (TH), but its safety and efficacy in obese patients remain underexplored.ObjectiveThis study aimed to assess the impact of obesity on the perioperative and clinical outcomes of v-NOTES hysterectomy, accounting for potential confounders.

pmc-12471051.title: Cannulation Strategies for Aortic Arch Surgery
pmc-12471051.creator: Ishtiaq Rahman, Jason Ali, Ravi De Silva, Alan P Sawchuk
pmc-12471051.description: Aortic arch surgery remains associated with significant mortality and morbidity especially in the setting of acute type A aortic dissection. Adequate cerebral protection is essential, and several methods have been proposed to avoid neurological injury during aortic arch surgery. The most common techniques include selective antegrade perfusion of brachiocephalic arteries or an interval of deep hypothermic circulatory arrest.

pmc-12504456.title: Predicting the co-invasion of two Asteraceae plant genera in post-mining landscapes using satellite remote sensing and airborne LiDAR
pmc-12504456.creator: Kamil Kędra, Andrzej M Jagodziński
pmc-12504456.description: The Asteraceae plant family includes the most widespread weedy invaders in Europe, which may jointly inhibit natural succession in degraded land under restoration. The complex local drivers of co-invasions hinder remote sensing (RS) monitoring efforts, as the links between the ecological and the spectral habitat properties are largely unknown.

pmc-12864985.title: Aldehyde cool-flame chemistry explains a missing source of organic acids
pmc-12864985.creator: Bingzhi Liu, Bin Dong, Huanhuan Wang, Shanshan Ruan, Qingbo Zhu, Weiye Chen, Liuyuan Wang, Long Zhu, Lili Xing, Donald G. Truhlar, Zhandong Wang
pmc-12864985.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Combustion emission is a significant source of organic acids, impacting atmospheric chemistry and climate. Their formation mechanisms, however, remain poorly understood, leading to underestimation in kinetic models. We investigate the cool-flame oxidation of key combustion intermediates—C1–C4 aldehydes and benzaldehyde. Using in-situ synchrotron vacuum ultraviolet photoionization mass spectrometry, we observe the direct conversion of aldehydes to organic acids, a process enhanced by HO2 radicals.

pmc-13081677.title: Comparative performance of large language models and Drugs.com versus Lexicomp for antiseizure medication drug–drug interactions: A cross-sectional study with iterative prompting analysis
pmc-13081677.creator: Maazuddin Mohammed, Mohammed Amer Khan, Vaibhav Chaudhary, Hamzeh Alsaleh, Syeda Bushra Fatima, Biplab Pal
pmc-13081677.description: BackgroundAntiseizure medications (ASMs) are frequently co-prescribed and are associated with a high risk of clinically significant drug–drug interactions (DDIs). Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for clinical queries, yet their performance in detecting ASM-related DDIs compared with established drug interaction databases remains uncertain.

pmc-13150456.title: Comprehensive Understanding and Diagnostic Approaches to Acute Right Ventricular Failure in the CCU
pmc-13150456.creator: Jung Sun Cho
pmc-13150456.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). stic that underscores the high prevalence of RV dysfunction in critical care settings. It is now well-established that the presence of RV dysfunction is not merely a clinical finding but a critical determinant of poor patient prognosis.1,2) The pathophysiology of RV failure in the intensive care unit is multifactorial, involving excess preload, bradycardia, increased pulmonary artery (PA) pressure or pulmonary vascular resistance, concomitant left ventricular (LV) failure, and increased afterload secondary to mechanical ventilation.

pmc-13365362.title: A Novel Public Dataset for Strawberry (Fragaria × Ananassa) Ripeness Detection and Comparative Evaluation of YOLO‐Based Models
pmc-13365362.creator: Mustafa Yurdakul, Zeynep Sena Baştuğ, Ali Emre Gök, Şakir Taşdemir
pmc-13365362.description: The strawberry (Fragaria × ananassa), known worldwide for its economic value and nutritional richness, is a widely cultivated fruit. Determining the correct ripeness level during the harvest period is crucial for both preventing losses for producers and ensuring consumers receive a quality product.
